title: Enumerate Primes
statement:
Return every prime number not greater than an upper bound.

Contract
- `upperBound` may be any `int`. Values below `2` produce an empty array.
- Return the primes in strictly increasing order.
- A prime is an integer greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and itself.
- Do not use probabilistic primality tests.

Examples
- `enumeratePrimes(1)` returns `[]`.
- `enumeratePrimes(10)` returns `[2, 3, 5, 7]`.
- `enumeratePrimes(20)` returns `[2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19]`.
hints: Try marking every composite number rather than testing divisibility from scratch for each value.
Once `p * p` is beyond the bound, every remaining unmarked value is prime.
Use a sieve: when a prime is found, mark multiples starting at its square. Intended complexity: O(n) to O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: an inclusive upper bound, for example: 20
